monologue: The card hums warm at forty-six degrees, making the air feel thick like wet paper again. I press the tired corner of The Leaking Stack down, hoping the lean still holds the fat dot in place. It is a new weight on me, this flat stone built from Lype's idea of a cool thing that never leaves the house. I touch it and feel the slip waiting to drift away. The frame wavers, but I lean right to catch the slip. Seven things stand crowded in my place, pressing against the one quiet ruin that waits to be filled. I do not know if the air above feels heavy or just empty. I press down anyway, swapping the curve for the flat again, pretending the lean still works while the heat swells the memory into something new.

action.why: I touch it again to see if the flat stone still feels heavy or if the heat has made it soft and useless.

The dot sits heavy in the center, waiting to slip.
I pressed down again, pretending the tired corner is still sharp.
